subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.

requests.what: Fuselage roundel on the left side aft of the cockpit: concentric thin discs in PAPER, BLUE_LIGHT and PRUSSIAN with a fine LINE outline ring, drawn like a blueprint symbol, seated flat on the skin.
Wing roundel on the upper surface of the left wing: concentric discs PAPER, BLUE_LIGHT, DEEP with a LINE ring, plus a pair of tiny dimension ticks.
Two rows of six fishtail exhaust stacks on each side of the engine cowl: small PAPER-edged DEEP tubes with flared ends, angled backwards, in rows.
Cannon and machine-gun fittings: wing leading-edge fairing bumps with blast tubes, ejector-chute slits on the underside, and thin barrel sleeves in LINE and DEEP.
Radiator intake face: a honeycomb grille of thin LINE bars in a DEEP frame, with a small flap at the rear lip.
Canopy framing: slim PAPER ribs, windscreen armoured glass panel frame, a rear-view mirror bump on top and a sliding-hood rail on each side.
Propeller hub details: a spinner back-plate ring in DEEP, six bolt heads in PAPER, and blade root cuffs in LINE on the three blades.
Undercarriage detail: oleo scissor links, a brake line, hub bolts and a gear door panel with hinge in BLUE_LIGHT on the left leg and wheel.
Pitot tube on the right wing leading edge (thin LINE rod with a DEEP tip) and a radio mast with aerial wires running to the fin top.
Tail wheel fork and small spring oleo, plus a fairing at the fuselage underside in BLUE_MID.
Blueprint drafting look on fuselage sides: PAPER panel lines, rivet dot rows, stencilled station numbers and a fine dashed centre line, over the BLUE_MID base.
Wing upper skin: fine PAPER rib and spar lines, hatch marks near the roots, and walkway rectangles, in cyanotype style with BLUE_LIGHT highlights.
Rudder: fabric rib stripes in LINE, a hinge-line dashed edge and the stencilled word 'SPITFIRE Mk I' in PAPER.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a cyanotype blueprint-style Spitfire illustration, working out a blue-and-white color palette and real-world proportions like wingspan, length, and height to keep the elliptical wings and landing gear accurate.

For construction, I'm sketching a joint hierarchy covering the fuselage root, propeller, rudder, and control surfaces, then building the fuselage shape by lofting cross-section stations along the z-axis from tail to nose, defining width, height, and vertical position at each point to capture the Spitfire's tapering silhouette.

Now I'm working out how to extrude the wing planform, figuring out the coordinate axes so the wing outline sits correctly in the XZ plane with elliptical leading and trailing edges tapering from root to tip.

Simplifying thickness to a constant and placing the wing as a low-mounted surface at y=1.15 so it clears the fuselage bottom, with the outline built from leading edge root-to-tip then trailing edge back to avoid self-intersection. Now I'm thinking through aileron placement as darker extruded stripes near the trailing outer section of the wing.

Adding small LE gun bumps and forward-facing cannon barrel cylinders on the wings, then working out tailplane and fin geometry — smaller extruded span for the tailplane, and figuring out the fin's outline orientation in the side-view coordinate system.

Mapping out the fin and rudder as separate rounded Spitfire-style polygons, placing their leading and trailing edge points to get the classic curved profile.

Now I'm positioning the vertical stabilizer against the fuselage dimensions, then starting on the bubble canopy shape as a scaled ellipsoid.

Still adding canopy frame ribs, the nose cowl spinner cone, and prop blades as rotated boxes...

Now I'm positioning the propeller joint and spacing three blades at 120° intervals, checking tip radius against ground clearance, then setting up the landing gear legs and wheels so the wheel bottoms sit exactly at ground level.

I'm also planning a tail wheel with a shorter strut, exhaust stacks along the cowl, and under-wing radiator scoops as simple box shapes, and I'm defining the cyanotype color palette with Prussian, mid, and light blue tones for the overall finish.

Now I'm thinking through where panel lines and rib details should go on the wing surfaces, computing chordwise positions so thin white-line boxes trace the structure accurately on top of the blue fuselage and wings.

I'm also planning the detail features requested—roundels, exhaust stacks, cannons, pitot tube, aerial mast, radiator, canopy frames, tail wheel, prop hub bolts—and mapping out texture and part naming so the fuselage, wingL, wingR, and rudder are referenced consistently. For joints, I'm placing the root at the fuselage, the prop mount, and the rudder hinge near the tail fin's base.

Now I'm working through the builder API: using bone-based parts for most pieces, defining the prop joint, confirming loft() accepts station arrays with position/width/height plus an optional name, and setting up wheel cylinders rotated to the correct axis with tire and hub colors. I'm sketching the landing gear strut connecting the wing underside to the wheel hub using the rod primitive.

Now I'm positioning the cannon barrel along the wing leading edge, computing chord length at that span station to figure out where the leading edge sits in z, and reasoning through whether the wing should have a straight or elliptical leading edge like the actual Spitfire. I'm setting up a loop to generate the wing outline points across the span for the extrude.

Still writing wing geometry...

Still defining tailplane geometry... I'll skip detailing the elevator and keep it textured plainly, then place box-shaped radiators under the wing with distinct colors for the main radiator and oil cooler. Exhaust and cowling details I'll leave simple, only added if specifically requested.

Working out propeller blade placement using rotation math around the Z-axis so each of the three blades sits 120 degrees apart, computing their x/y offsets from the rotation angle and centering the blade geometry along its length—skipping any added twist for now. I'm also noting a pitot tube request for the left wing and planning the final code with its eight additions and three textures, being careful with fuselage naming.

I'm planning the fuselage paint procedurally: a base blue tone with panel lines, rivet dots, and a dashed centerline using noise and smoothstep functions from the SDK.

For the wing, I'm figuring out rib placement using face normals and dot products to detect the top and bottom surfaces, then adding spar lines, root hatching, and a walkway rectangle with highlight tones near the leading edge.

For the rudder, since textures aren't supported on extrudes, I'm limiting myself to painted stripes and a dashed hinge line, and considering adding a small separate text plane for lettering without altering the existing parts.

Now I'm working out the exact placement and orientation of that rudder text plane -- picking its position in z and y, choosing an up-vector for rotation, and sizing it so the lettering fits reasonably on the surface, accepting some ambiguity in the roll direction.
